questions.q: A script on the companion doesn't receive replies addressed to it. The most common cause:
options: Bad CRC in the autopilot's replies
questions.explain: The route to its compid appears after the first packet from the addressee.

questions.q: A broadcast message (target_system = 0) is forwarded by the autopilot:
options: To all ports except the input one
Only to the port with the GCS on it

questions.q: Why is UDP better than TCP for telemetry over 4G?
options: TCP holds fresh data behind old data
UDP encrypts data at the protocol level
questions.explain: Head-of-line blocking: under loss TCP retransmits old data and holds back fresh data.

questions.q: A vehicle with a 4G modem behind the carrier's NAT. How do you connect to it from the GCS?
options: Open a port on the modem
questions.explain: Incoming connections to a private IP are impossible.

questions.q: The typical compid of an onboard computer:
Two GCSs with sysid 255 on the same network lead to:
options: Automatic selection of the primary GCS

questions.q: Disable MAVLink forwarding through a port in ArduPilot 4.7+:
What do you use to reproduce a bad network on Linux without a radio?
QGroundControl on the laptop stopped seeing the vehicle as soon as the script was started. Configuration:
questions.fragment:
SITL: --out udp:127.0.0.1:14550
QGC: listens on UDP 14550
script.py: mavutil.mavlink_connection('udpin:0.0.0.0:14550')
options: The script and QGC listen on the same UDP port 14550: you need a second SITL output (14551) or a router
udpin in the script grabs sysid 255, and QGC drops the vehicle as foreign
QGC requires MAVLink 1 on port 14550, and pymavlink switched the whole SITL stream to MAVLink 2
SITL sends data only to the first client to connect over TCP 5760
questions.explain: One UDP port — one listener; split the streams with a router or separate outputs.
